title: review follow-ups of PR #37655: scaffold-e2e tarball job coverage and stale wording
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czzx9dtSEm3jWWL9c3

Filing gate: owed follow-ups of review work (L1/L2 exception: one `review follow-ups of PR #N` card per PR, items ticked). Source: fleet. Found in the contract review of PR #37655 (card #37441), record 7203561225.

Grading: area:fleet · Task · CI-gate coverage and comment accuracy, no product behaviour → suggested p3 · evidence: read on the PR head `3ded0a66` and its job log 140079805119.

## Items

- [ ] **The tarball job runs too rarely for what it now tests.** After #37655, `Scaffold with repo dist` installs the whole framework closure of the checkout, but `on.pull_request.paths` names only `packages/create-objectstack/**`, `docker/**` and the workflow, and the job has `if: github.event_name != 'schedule'`. A framework PR that breaks the scaffolded project is first seen on the next unrelated template or Docker PR, which is the stall #37441 was filed to end. `os-create-smoke.yml` covers the same gap with a nightly run. Options: a nightly run of this job, or `paths:` naming the packer `scripts/publish-smoke-pack.mjs`. This changes an existing gate's trigger (governed `.github/workflows/**`, Tier H), so whoever picks it up checks the gate rule first. Re-check: `sed -n '27,36p;50,52p' .github/workflows/scaffold-e2e.yml`.
- [ ] **The pinned-shape step's warning string is stale.** It still says "the unpublished-version window the install step's fallback exists for (that fallback lives in this workflow…)", and its comment heading reads "WHY IT STILL LIVES HERE". No install-step fallback exists after #37655, and the warning printed in that head's run. #37441 Scope 3 froze the step's commands, so it was left as is. Re-check: `grep -n "install step's fallback" .github/workflows/scaffold-e2e.yml`.
- [ ] **The project install uses whatever pnpm Corepack finds.** A bare `pnpm install` in a directory with no `packageManager` field fetched pnpm 12.x in the job, while the scaffolded Dockerfile reads that lockfile with `pnpm@10` and the template's CI pins 10. It follows the `scripts/create-scaffold-smoke.sh` precedent and works today. A cross-major lockfile hand-off can still red the job for a reason unrelated to the PR. Either name the choice in a comment or pin the major. Re-check: `grep -n "pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile" .github/workflows/scaffold-e2e.yml`.

## Business reason

The job is the first-run gate for `npm create objectstack`: it should catch a framework change that breaks a new user's project on the PR that makes it, and its comments and warnings should describe what it actually does.

## Who acts

The seat that owns `.github/workflows/scaffold-e2e.yml` changes (Tier H; today seat repo:objectstack#1, area o1-A, after triage's first touch).

Dedupe: `review follow-ups of PR #37655` → 0 open; `scaffold-e2e paths schedule` → 3 open hits: #37441 (the parent, closing with #37655) and two seat posts; no open card on this trigger.

Parent: objectstack-ai/objectstack#37441.
